extra.message: SQL injection: the URL route parameter pageId (from /dashboard/<pageId> in controllers/Dashboard.py:8) is concatenated directly into the SQL string 'SELECT pageId, title, content FROM pages WHERE pageId='+pageId and executed via db.execute(). No parameterization or validation is performed, allowing UNION-based SQL injection to read/modify arbitrary database contents.

Reflected XSS: the user-supplied 'search' form field is passed to render_template('search/index.html', search=search). The template renders it with {% autoescape false %}{{search}}{% endautoescape %} (templates/search/index.html:13), so attacker-controlled HTML/JavaScript is returned unescaped. The response also explicitly disables the browser filter via X-XSS-Protection: 0 (line 11).

Stored XSS: the user-supplied 'link' value is stored unvalidated (controllers/Messaging.py:16,19 -> models/Messaging.py:13) and rendered into an href attribute (<a href="{{item[3]}}">). Although Jinja2 escapes quotes, it does not block the javascript: URI scheme, so an attacker can store a payload such as javascript:alert(document.cookie) that executes when a victim clicks the link.

Command injection: the template context processor exposes system_call(command) which runs os.popen(command).read() with no sanitisation. Because the function is registered as a Jinja2 global it can be invoked from any template expression, e.g. the 404 handler's render_template_string reaches it via /{{system_call('id')}}, allowing arbitrary OS command execution.

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI): the 404 handler builds a Jinja2 template with .format(request.url) and then calls render_template_string(template). The raw request URL (which can contain {{...}}) is inserted into the template before rendering, so a request such as /{{system_call('id')}} is evaluated by Jinja2, leading to arbitrary command execution/RCE.

Insecure deserialization: the /about/sync handler reads the attacker-controlled form field data_obj, hex-decodes it (line 22-23), writes it to ../pickle.hacker and then calls pickle.load(handle). Untrusted pickle data allows arbitrary code execution via a crafted __reduce__ payload (e.g. os.system).

Insecure deserialization: the /information/<input> route base64-decodes the user-controlled path segment and passes it to yaml.load() without a Loader. PyYAML's default loader can instantiate arbitrary Python objects, so a payload such as yaml: !!python/object/apply:os.system ["id"] results in arbitrary command execution.

XML External Entity (XXE) injection: request.form['customers'] is parsed with xml.dom.pulldom.parseString(), which expands external entities. A crafted XML document with a DOCTYPE declaring an external entity (e.g. SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd") can read local files or perform SSRF. Use defusedxml instead.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: Path traversal / arbitrary file read: /validator/getXML takes the filename directly from request.form['example_file'] (line 29), opens it with open(fileName) (line 30) and serves it with send_file(fileName) (line 31) without validating against a base directory. A value like ../../etc/passwd or ../../project/config/sqlite.py allows reading arbitrary server files.

Unrestricted file upload: /validator/uploads only checks the extension via allowed_file() and then saves the client-supplied filename directly as 'uploads/'+filename. The filename is not sanitised, so path traversal (../../) can write outside the uploads directory, and allowed extensions such as .html can be used to plant stored XSS content.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: Authentication bypass: the /webmaster route has no authentication check and unconditionally sets session['loggedin'] = random for any visitor. This backdoor grants access to the protected /confidential page (which only checks session['loggedin']) without knowing any credentials.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Hardcoded credentials: authentication is performed by comparing the submitted username and password against the hardcoded plaintext values "admin"/"admin" instead of verifying against a credential store with hashed passwords.

Hardcoded secret key: app.config['SECRET_KEY'] = 'random' is a weak, hardcoded value. It is used to sign Flask session cookies, so an attacker who knows it can forge arbitrary sessions (including setting loggedin) and bypass authentication.

Security misconfiguration: app.debug = True enables the Werkzeug debugger in production. The interactive debugger console can lead to remote code execution if the debug PIN is obtained, and exposes detailed stack traces/source.

CORS misconfiguration: CORS(app, resources={r"/*": {"origins": "*"}}) allows every origin. Combined with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true set on /confidential (controllers/Confidential.py:10), any malicious website can issue credentialed XHR requests and read sensitive authenticated responses.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: Sensitive data exposure: the webmaster template hardcodes plaintext credentials (e.g. Mark/Thisismysecretpass) and is rendered by the unauthenticated /webmaster route (controllers/Webmaster.py:11), disclosing reusable passwords to any visitor.

Use of weak password hashing: seed data stores user passwords as unsalted MD5 hashes (0cef1fb10f60529028a71f58e54ed07b, etc.). MD5 is fast and unsalted, allowing trivial offline brute-force/rainbow-table cracking of the credentials.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
